title: Polyglot cursor adapter and streaming ergonomics for embeddings + rerank
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a cross-language CursorAdapter and streaming ergonomics to provide API parity for embeddings + reranking endpoints across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Deliver helpers for pagination + batching (cursor, page_size, prefetching, and backpressure) and durable, testable retry semantics for partial-batch failures. Provide canonical examples and migration notes for existing iterator helpers.
acceptance_criteria: Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs expose a CursorAdapter that supports stable opaque cursors, next_page() / stream() ergonomics, and deterministic ordering for rerank results.
Cross-language integration tests validate identical behavior for: page sizes, cursor roundtrips, prefetching window, max-concurrency, and retry-on-partial-failure semantics.

Batching helpers automatically coalesce small requests into BatchShard windows without violating latency SLOs (p95 < 200ms for 1-4 token embedding calls in local harness) except when explicitly disabled.
Retry profiles: transient network + 5xx retriable, idempotent-safe for embeddings and reranking; documented and covered by unit tests.
Examples: one notebook/example per language demonstrating embeddings pagination, incremental rerank streaming with backpressure, and an example of migration from legacy iterator APIs.
Docs updated (SDK reference + migration guide) and a public example repo with tests passing on CI (Linux + macOS).

decisions: Use opaque base64 cursor token that encodes: (cursor_version, last_id, batch_offset, checksum). Keeps server freedom to change internals while enabling client resume.
Streaming API will provide two ergonomic surfaces: a synchronous iterator (next_page) and an async/streaming path (on_item/on_batch) in languages that support async semantics.
Retry default will be conservative: retry only idempotent-safe operations (embeddings & rerank request bodies must include client-provided request_id to allow de-dupe on server).
Prefetch default window: 2 pages ahead with max inflight 3; configurable per-client. Backpressure is applied by pausing prefetch if consumer can't drain within 200ms.
Cursor versioning: include version byte to allow future migration; server will return HTTP 410 for incompatible cursors with migration hint link.

notes: Migration note: legacy iterator helpers (legacy_iter* APIs) will be deprecated in next minor; provide adapter shim for one release cycle.

Design trade-off: opaque cursor avoids leaking internal sequence numbers to clients but increases difficulty for debugging; we will include a debug_endpoint that emits a human-readable decoding under admin perms.
